title: Why AI Can't Count the R's in 'Strawberry' (Tokens Explained)
audience: Anyone who uses ChatGPT/Claude; junior devs paying per-token API bills
whyCare: Tokens decide what AI can 'see' and what it costs; the strawberry meme is an instantly recognisable hook.

angle: The word 'strawberry' splits into token blocks (illustrative split, labelled 'example'); the model only sees token IDs (code panel of numbers). Stat counter: ~4 characters per token rule of thumb (cite OpenAI tokenizer docs). Payoff: that's also why you pay per token.
hook: Ask AI how many R's are in 'strawberry'. It used to get it wrong. Here's why.
strengths: Meme-level hook + clean visual; cheap (code panel + diagram); evergreen
weaknesses: Newer models often answer correctly, so phrase as 'used to / still can on harder words'; exact split varies by tokenizer (must be labelled illustrative)
